biggest_catch: The resolution sets flat per-election pay but does not state shift hours or when/how pay is issued.
catches: Flat per-election pay regardless of how long the day runs.
Training pays only $20 per class attended.
Constable pay ($110) is a separate Election Day role under the Election Code.
County resolution does not publish shift hours or payment timing — hours below are an honest PA-standard estimate.

c1.evidence: Official Lancaster County, PA Election Board Resolution No. 3 of 2024, adopted 2024-02-28 (co.lancaster.pa.us).

c2.evidence: 'total compensation for judges of elections for each election is fixed at Two Hundred Dollars ($200.00)'; inspectors $175; clerks/machine inspectors $150 ($75 half-day); training $20.

c3.evidence: No fee to apply or serve.

c4.evidence: No risk capital; flat government stipends.

eligibility: Lancaster County PA voter; judges/inspectors serve as district election officers per PA Election Code; attend training.
notes: Lancaster County, PA — rank ~104-110 by population. Rates from Election Board Resolution No. 3 (2024), the county's current official compensation schedule (no newer schedule published). Range excludes constable ($110), a separate office. The resolution does not publish shift hours; PA polls are open 7 a.m.-8 p.m. and workers report before opening and stay for closing, so time is estimated on that standard.
numeric_basis: payout from official county resolution (Res. No. 3, 2024): $150 clerk/machine inspector / $175 inspector / $200 judge, $20 training; time: PA-standard full Election Day ~6:00 a.m.-9:00 p.m. (~15 hrs) plus training (~2 h)
payout_quote: The total compensation for judges of elections for each election is fixed at Two Hundred Dollars ($200.00).
payout_value_note: Flat per-election stipend by election-board role: $200 judge of elections, $175 majority/minority inspector, $150 clerk/machine inspector ($75 half-day); $20 training. Constable ($110) excluded — not a poll-worker role.

steps: Confirm eligibility as a Lancaster County PA voter for a district election officer role.
Contact the Lancaster County Board of Elections to apply or fill a vacancy.
Attend the training class provided by the Board ($20).
Work the full election as judge, inspector, clerk, machine inspector, or constable.
timing: Election-day only (per election) plus training class.
